plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Shading down doesn't help since payment is determined by others' bids, not yours. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $47 to maximize expected profit.

In this second-price auction format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to shading my bid down - doing so only risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Bidding above my value risks negative profit. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $33, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay a fair price determined by the second-highest bidder.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit) and never miss out on profitable wins. There's no benefit to shading my bid here, unlike first-price auctions. I'll bid my true value of $36.
